newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: SRI LANKA STOCKS CLOSE UP ON RETAIL TRADE.
newsitem.headline: SRI LANKA STOCKS CLOSE UP ON RETAIL TRADE.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed higher on retail trade on Tuesday as institutional investors were on the sidelines ahead of third quarter results and new issues of plantation shares planned in September, brokers said.
The all-share index closed 2.4 points higher at 854.2. Price gains nudged out losses by 37 to 32. Ahungalla Hotel rose four rupees to 75, and Hatton National was up 10 to 300.

"Institutional investors are going slow because they believe the market is now in line with earnings up to June. They are waiting for the results to the end of September," said Deva Ellepola of brokerage Jardine Fleming HNB.
Turnover was 92.3 million rupees, with foreign buying at 11.8 million rupees and selling at 49.4 million.
"Foreign investors are probably waiting for the plantation initial public offers, which are expected to start in early September," said a trader at brokerage Asia Securities.
The Public Enterprise Reform Commission last month said it would begin rolling out from September IPOs of seven estate firms, in which 51 percent stakes were sold to strategic investors in 1996.
